valuation.method: Forward EPS x justified P/E: FY2027 diluted EPS, the year an investor at the Nov 2027 12-month target date is pricing, times a P/E. Anchors from the Q3 2026 release (Oct 22, 2026): adjusted diluted EPS $3.53 (reported $3.49), adjusted operating ratio 58.8%, 594.5M weighted diluted shares. Management kept its outlook of high-single-digit reported EPS growth for 2026, consistent with a 3-year EPS CAGR target of high-single to low-double digits through 2027 (company guidance, no dollar figure given). The FY2026 (about $12.47) and FY2027 (about $13.56, +9%) EPS levels are a third-party consensus from one aggregator (TIKR), not checked against a primary source; the bear and bull EPS are my assumptions around it. Market cap about $176-183B (aggregate row, USD, 594.25M shares at the $302.44 close), well above the $20B floor. Price targets exclude the dividend (annual rate $5.68 in the aggregate row, not added). Pending transactions, including the Norfolk Southern combination, are not modelled; the base assumes standalone earnings.

bear.driver: Volume softness and fuel-driven cost pressure (Q4 fuel guided to $4.85/gal vs $4.21 in Q3) leave 2027 EPS about 5% below consensus; the market pays a lower multiple for a slower-growth rail franchise

base.driver: Consensus-level 2027 EPS consistent with the management 3-year CAGR goal; operating ratio held near the 58-59% range; P/E trims from the current 22.3x consensus-2027 multiple to 21x as growth normalises

bull.driver: Intermodal and pricing run ahead of the plan, OR gains continue, and buybacks lift per-share EPS about 6% above consensus; the premium multiple holds

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $13.56 the $302.44 close implies 22.3x. The aggregate analyst mean target ($329.96, 24 analysts, Yahoo Finance via yfinance) implies 24.3x at base EPS, or about $15.71 EPS at 21x (about 16% above base). The named-firm targets above ($310 to $339) sit mostly in that range.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $13.56 (4.5 pp of the close); $1.00 of 2027 EPS moves it by $21.00 (6.9 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Reported EPS growth and operating ratio in Q4 2026 and the 2027 outlook: the base case needs roughly 9% EPS growth in 2027 with the OR in the high 50s. Fuel above the $4.85/gal Q4 assumption, or volume declines, would move the case toward the bear.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year 2026 results, expected around late January 2027 (exact date not confirmed in the sources)

analyst_notes: Named coverage is thin: only Baird (Dan Moore) has an identifiable sequence in the window. Baird raised to $344 with an Outperform rating on Jul 27, 2026, then cut to $310 with a Neutral rating on Nov 5, 2026, the latest named view. UBS upgraded to Buy with a $339 target on Sep 16, 2026, and JPMorgan (Neutral, $334) moved on Jul 24, 2026; both analysts are unnamed in the sources. The firm-level targets ($310 to $339) are 2.5 to 12 percent above the close, against a base case at -5.8 percent. At our $13.56 base EPS they imply 22.9x to 25.0x, 2 to 4 turns above our 21x; equivalently, about $1.20 to $2.60 more 2027 EPS at 21x. The gap is therefore a multiple or earnings-growth question that the broker models do not disclose. Aggregate mean and median targets ($330 and $335) are provider data (Yahoo Finance via yfinance, 24 analysts) and are not in the weighted target; the wide spread between aggregators (about $280 to $330) reflects stale or undated entries.
